title: What a docent is
content: Docent is a bounded automated guide to an explicitly configured collection. It answers from public typed records and does not impersonate an author, maintainer, or person described by the collection.

title: The bounded chat request path
content: For each single-user chat message, the FastAPI gateway retrieves a bounded set of public typed records, combines them with a bounded recent transcript and a fixed behavior contract, invokes the selected provider, validates its response envelope, removes unsupported or duplicate source IDs, and returns one answer.

title: Bounded source jurisdiction
content: Docent differs from unrestricted chat-with-a-document because its evidence is a validated collection of typed records with explicit authority, confidence, answer policy, and boundaries. If retrieved public records do not support an answer, Docent reports the limitation instead of silently filling the gap from general knowledge.
question_forms: How is this different from chat with a PDF?

title: Typed epistemic records
content: Each DocentRecord has a stable ID, record and subject types, title, content, question forms, topics, entities, a typed source locator, boundaries, an answer policy, confidence, and version. Corpus loading validates every JSONL row and rejects duplicate record IDs.
question_forms: What is a typed epistemic record?

title: Source authority and confidence
content: Deterministic retrieval applies authored weights for primary, official, contextual, and commentary authority and for authoritative, high, medium, low, and unknown confidence. These weights adjust lexical ranking; they do not convert evidence into certainty or make the model an authority.
question_forms: How do authority and confidence work?

title: Deterministic bounded retrieval
content: The default retriever uses deterministic BM25-style lexical relevance with exact question-form, topic, and entity boosts. Public search filters non-public records before scoring and returns at most the configured retrieval limit in deterministic order.

title: Validated response envelopes
content: Providers must return a strict envelope containing reply, record_ids, grounded, and limitations. The gateway rejects malformed envelopes, removes invented and duplicate record IDs, and forces grounded to false when no valid supporting ID remains.

title: Provider separation and mock mode
content: Model completion is behind a small provider protocol. Deterministic mock mode requires no API key and returns the top retrieved public record without synthesis. The OpenAI-compatible provider is selected by configuration and sends prompts server-side; browser code never receives a provider credential.
question_forms: Where is the model key used?

title: Gateway and runtime separation
content: The gateway owns public retrieval, input bounds, response validation, and HTTP contracts. AgentRuntime is a protocol seam for later mediated execution, but no room-to-runtime orchestration or external runtime adapter is implemented. The shared-room endpoints must not be presented as a working agent room.
question_forms: Is the shared agent room working?
Is there an external agent runtime?

title: Public, restricted, and refusal records
content: Public endpoints use only records whose answer_policy is public. Restricted and refuse-extraction records are excluded by gateway retrieval code before prompts, search responses, and mock responses are built. A future trusted internal path must be called explicitly and is not exposed by the public API.
boundaries: No restricted metadata or hit counts in public APIs

title: Single-user chat and partial room transport
content: POST /api/chat is the working bounded single-user path. The /api/room endpoints provide in-memory message insertion, cursor and epoch semantics, idempotency, bounded history, and a bounded pending-turn queue, but they do not run an agent or produce agent replies.
boundaries: Do not claim agent room execution

title: Local, Docker, Pages, and Space deployment
content: The same FastAPI application can run locally or in a Docker container on port 7860. The canonical static client can be served by FastAPI or GitHub Pages and can call a configured public API URL. A Hugging Face Docker Space can host the API and mock provider without a model secret.
question_forms: Does it run on Hugging Face?
boundaries: Live public deployment is not claimed until observed

title: Creating another docent
content: To create another docent, author a subject-neutral or domain-specific public JSONL corpus that validates against DocentRecord, update the identity and jurisdiction contract, test representative questions and refusal boundaries, and select deployment configuration through environment variables. Do not place secrets in records or frontend files.
question_forms: How do I create another docent?
How do I author a corpus?

title: Self-describing development pathways
content: Docent stores capabilities, possible pathways, human decisions, and experiments as strict manifests. A deterministic frontier derives admissible and blocked pathways from declared preconditions and exposes qualitative Bellman-style pressures such as value, cost, risk, reversibility, and future option value. It computes no aggregate score and humans select every pathway.
boundaries: Metaphor and design structure, not mathematical optimization

title: OmegaClaw inspiration and boundary
content: Public-agent experiments using OmegaClaw informed some development questions and the project preserves attribution to OmegaClaw's creators. OmegaClaw is not bundled, connected, or running in this repository; an adapter is only a possible future pathway.

title: What is deliberately not included
content: This repository contains no deleted subject-specific atlas, former hosted-space identity, private token, conference-specific corpus, paper-specific corpus, production frontend framework, durable database, WebSocket agent transport, external runtime adapter, or true multi-user agent execution.
boundaries: Do not reconstruct deleted subject matter

title: Live and deterministic inference modes
content: Docent can use live model inference or deterministic corpus mode. Live mode asks a configured server-side provider to synthesize from bounded public evidence. Deterministic mode returns retrieved corpus evidence without model inference. A live failure never silently becomes a deterministic answer; the visitor must explicitly choose deterministic mode.

title: OpenRouter reference gateway
content: The public reference deployment can use OpenRouter through Docent's generic OpenAI-compatible provider. The operator selects an opaque model route with DOCENT_MODEL; changing that value does not require a code change. openrouter/free is a router route, so the actual responding model may vary and is reported separately when the provider supplies it. OpenRouter is optional and does not own or endorse Docent.

title: Gateway-owned inference provenance
content: Docent's gateway—not the model—states whether a response used live or deterministic inference, the configured provider route, the actual responding model when known, grounding status, supporting record identifiers, and limitations. The gateway locally validates every response envelope and removes unsupported source identifiers before publication.
question_forms: How do I know which model answered?
boundaries: Model cannot author provenance or evidence authorization

title: Process-local live inference budget
content: The demo reserves one application budget unit before each live provider attempt, including attempts that fail upstream. Deterministic requests and requests rejected before an upstream attempt do not consume it. The counter resets at the UTC day boundary and on process restart, is not durable or correct across replicas, and is only a demo safeguard. The external provider remains the authoritative outer limit; current free-tier availability and limits must be checked in current provider documentation.
